title: Pasted derived direct-image unit on K-flat Hom tests
statement: Let f:X\to Y and g:Y\to Z be morphisms of ringed spaces [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Let I be a K-injective cochain complex of O_X-modules [def-pur-kinjective-complex] and K a K-flat cochain complex of O_Z-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Use the module direct images, derived direct images and right-derived units of [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], and write Q for localization. Postcomposition with the pasted unit induces a bijection Hom_{D(O_Z)}(QK,Q(g_*f_*I)) → Hom_{D(O_Z)}(QK,Rg_*Rf_*QI), sending a to a ≫ η_g(f_*I) ≫ Rg_*(η_f(I)). This assertion is only for localized K-flat test complexes, and imposes no boundedness or flatness on f or g.

source.place: lemma-adjoint (079W), lemma-derived-pullback-composition (0D5S), and the mate calculation in the argument of lemma-derived-pushforward-composition (0D5T)

proof.text: For a K-flat complex K on Z, successive tensor pullbacks along g and f remain K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-pullback-preservation]. They therefore compute Lf* Lg* QK for the derived pullbacks supplied by [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint-general]. No pullback-composition identification is needed for this Hom test.

The induced derived adjunctions and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identify Hom(QK,Rg* Rf* QI) with Hom_H(f* g* K,I). To identify localized maps QK→Q(g* f* I), represent one by a roof K ←s K′ →a g* f* I and resolve K′ by a K-flat K″ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The new s has K-flat endpoints; successive derived pullback shows its tensor pullback is a quasi-isomorphism. Take the underived adjunct b:f* g* K″→I and form Q(b) after the inverse of Q(f* g* s). K-injectivity gives a unique homotopy class f* g* K→I. Naturality makes it invariant under roof refinements. Its underived adjunct localized is inverse to this construction: after precomposition with s it is homotopic to a, because the adjuncts agree in the derived category and localization is faithful for maps into I. Common roof refinements prove injectivity as well as surjectivity. K-flatness is not confused with K-projectivity.

Use the counit compatibility of the derived adjunction induced from the underived adjunction [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived], twice. Taking adjuncts shows that the Hom identification just constructed sends a to a followed by ηg(f* I) followed by Rg*(ηf(I)). This is the pasted-unit mate calculation of Stacks 079W and 0D5T. Hence precisely the displayed postcomposition function is bijective.

theorem moduleDirectImage_pastedUnit_kFlat_hom_bijective
    {X Y Z : RingedSpace.{u}}
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wY} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wZ} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Z))]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X)) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective]
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Z)) ℤ) (hK : K.IsKFlat) :
    Function.Bijective (fun
      (a : DerivedCategory.Q.obj K ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh.obj
        (((moduleDirectImage g).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
          (((moduleDirectImage f).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
            ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I)))) =>
      a ≫ (moduleDirectImage g).rightDerivedFunctorUnit.app
          (((moduleDirectImage f).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
            ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I)) ≫
        (derivedModuleDirectImage g).map
          ((moduleDirectImage f).rightDerivedFunctorUnit.app
            ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I)))
